newsitem.title: USA: Leaders of Miami worker unions agree to cuts.
newsitem.headline: Leaders of Miami worker unions agree to cuts.

text.p: Leaders of Miami's four employee unions have agreed to accept $25 million worth of concessions over two years to help the city close its $68 million budget gap, assistant city manager Bill Hampton said Thursday.
Union members will vote on the agreements during the weekend and results should be known on Monday.
The concessions included cuts in wages and overtime pay, and agreements by the police officers to pay the city for off-duty use of city-owned cars.

The agreement came after union leaders spent weeks poring over city financial reports with their accountants to verify the city's claim that it has a $68 million deficit in the $275 million budget for the year that began Oct 1.
"They recognized that this is the truth and that it is needed to keep the city out of bankruptcy," Hampton said.

About $14 million of the concessions will be borne by the city's police officers, its largest employee group. Firefighters will bear $7 million of the burden and the remaining $4 million in cuts will come from sanitation workers and general employees.
